speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure 135/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Neck Examination: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node observed. Abdominal Examination: Slight abdominal distension; normal bowel sounds; dullness over the left lower quadrant; splenomegaly detected without rebound tenderness. Blood Work: Complete Blood Count shows Elevated WBC, Slightly Decreased Hemoglobin, and Normal Platelets; Lactate Dehydrogenase is Elevated. Imaging (CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen): Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy (Cervical Lymph Node): Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the CD20-positive biopsy and the presence of B-symptoms with widespread lymphadenopathy, your condition is highly consistent with a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. I have sufficient information to confirm the diagnosis without further questions. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
